title: FP8/INT8 kernel benchmarking sprint epic (runtime perf suite + rollout decisions)
creator: Talia Benson
content:
Epic goal
Deliver a defensible, reproducible FP8/INT8 benchmark matrix across top hosted models and primary fleet GPUs (H100, A100, plus at least one cost SKU where feasible), then translate results into concrete runtime changes: kernel auto-selection heuristics, scheduler knob defaults, and hosted-catalog quantization profile guidance. Changes must be safe to roll out via flags + perf canary with automatic rollback.

Why this sprint
We have kernel-level wins from FP8/INT8 paths that are not consistently realized end-to-end due to scheduling interactions (prefill/decode mix, batching window, backpressure) and shape-specific constraints. We also need reproducibility improvements (driver/CUDA pinning, clock locking, artifact metadata) so results are defensible internally (and selectively externally via PM).

Owners / stakeholders
- Program driver: Talia Benson
- Kernel lead: Hiro Tanaka (primary assignee)
- Scheduling lead: Sofia Ivanova
- Benchmark harness owner: Rina Kobayashi
- Perf/Evals decision owner: Jonas Weber
- Infra capacity sponsor: Neha Kapoor
- SRE canary/rollout owner: Rafael Mendes
- Observability/dashboards: Allison Grant

Scope (in)
1) Benchmark harness updates (microbench + E2E serving)
- Add FP8/INT8 modes, consistent warmup/measurement loops, standardized artifact export and metadata (git SHA, container, CUDA/driver, clocks, model hash, config).
- Add scheduler instrumentation to isolate prefill vs decode and expose queue depth/backpressure for mixed workloads.

2) Execution: benchmark matrix runs
- GPUs: H100 + A100 as required; add one cost-focused SKU (L4) if the harness supports apples-to-apples + we can reserve time.
- Models: “top hosted models” (final list captured in sprint plan / benchmark suite v3). Include realistic workloads: prompt length distributions, prefill/decode mixes, batch sizes, and concurrency profiles.

3) Analysis + decisions
- Kernel-selection heuristics: when to pick FP8 vs INT8 vs baseline by GPU arch and shape regime; include guardrails and correctness fallbacks.
- Scheduler parameter tuning: batching window / backpressure defaults tuned so end-to-end realizes kernel wins without TTFT regressions.
- Quantization policy guidance: which models eligible for FP8 vs INT8 defaults; when eval sign-off is required; calibration requirements and known risks.

4) Shipping + rollout
- Implement changes behind flags; enable per-model/per-region cohorts.
- Perf canary gates: thresholds for TTFT/TPOT/tokens/s with noise handling; automatic rollback triggers.
- Release notes + runbook updates.

Out of scope (explicit)
- Re-architecting the scheduler (we are tuning knobs + instrumentation only).
- Publishing public benchmarks. PM will decide what can be shared and with what footnotes.
- Model training changes (this is serving/runtime only).

Definition of done
- Benchmark matrix produced with p50/p95 latency, throughput, variance (error bars), and cost proxies across the agreed GPU/model/workload set.
- Reproducibility: runners pin driver/CUDA and optionally lock clocks; artifacts include required metadata; reruns on the same setup reproduce within standards variance.
- ADR-level decision captured for kernel auto-selection heuristics + guardrails + fallback.
- Scheduler tuning validated against the benchmark suite to avoid TTFT regressions (or documented trade-offs + gating).
- Perf canary thresholds implemented and dashboards live; rollback triggers tested at least once in staging or via controlled degradation.
- Runtime 1.22.0 changes merged, flagged, and rolled out via canary; release notes drafted.

Milestones / timeline (sprint-style, ~2 weeks)
- Day 1–2: Kickoff + methodology sign-off; reserve GPU capacity; finalize model/workload list.
- Day 3–4: Harness updates + calibration runs; validate measurement stability; address variance.
- Day 5–9: Full benchmark execution across matrix; daily anomaly triage.
- Day 10–11: Analysis + decisions (kernel heuristics + scheduler knobs + quant policy).
- Day 12–14: Implementation + perf canary gates; staged rollout and documentation.

Key decisions (summary)
- Kernel selection follows ADR-019: prefer FP8 on H100 for eligible shapes unless long-context quality risk is flagged; INT8 used primarily where matmul shapes align and quality is stable; baseline is default fallback.
- Scheduler knobs adjusted to prevent TTFT spikes under mixed workloads; batching window capped in low-concurrency regimes; backpressure thresholds tuned to avoid decode starvation.
- Quantization defaults require Applied ML sign-off for specific model families and long-context workloads; canary gating remains mandatory for default flips.

Risks + mitigations logged during sprint
- Variance on H100 due to clock drift/thermal throttling and shared-node contention → mitigate by pinning clocks where permitted, enforcing exclusive allocation in runner, and tagging artifacts with clocks + thermals.
- Correctness failures for INT8 on specific shapes → shape guardrails + runtime fallback to baseline + unit tests.
- End-to-end TTFT regressions even when kernel microbench wins → add scheduler instrumentation, tune batching/backpressure, require canary TTFT/TPOT thresholds.
- Customer impact from capacity contention during benchmark windows → reservation plan guardrails + avoid Dedicated pools + explicit SRE/Infra coordination.

Comms cadence used
- Daily 15-min triage (runtime + applied ML + SRE rep) during matrix execution.
- End-of-week readout to performance stakeholders (Jonas/Neha/Aditya/Henry) with “what we can claim” caveats.
- Rollout coordination in #eng-releases for runtime-1.22.0 RC sign-off.

Notes / updates (condensed)
- 2026-02-10: Epic created after kickoff thread; sub-issues opened for harness, kernel flags, scheduler instrumentation, and canary gates.
- 2026-02-13: Calibration run found unacceptable variance on H100; pivoted to driver/CUDA pinning + clock lock support.
- 2026-02-17: First full matrix pass complete for H100; A100 in progress; INT8 correctness failure reproduced → added shape guardrails and reran affected cells.
- 2026-02-20: ADR heuristics review converged; implemented + started canary gating integration.
- 2026-02-24: Canary detected TTFT regression in a narrow prompt regime; auto-rollback triggered; issue triaged to launch overhead + scheduler mix; hotfix landed to disable FP8 for that shape cohort pending deeper kernel work.
- 2026-02-28: Final matrix + eval summary attached in Drive; runtime-1.22.0 release notes updated; epic marked Done.

Follow-ups (not in scope for this epic, but recommended)
- Add L4 coverage and validate INT8 wins in cost SKU regimes (requires updated runner support + reservations).
- Expand quality suite to include more structured-output/tool-calling long-context prompts where FP8 showed sensitivity.
- Extend perf canary baselines per region and add automated drift detection for driver updates.
